title: How to Make Avakaya at Home — Traditional Andhra Mango Pickle
excerpt: The soul of Andhra cooking: raw mangoes, mustard, Guntur chilli and cold-pressed oil — the way Babai makes it.
body:
Avakaya is not just a pickle — it is the soul of Andhra cooking. Start with firm raw mangoes cut into cubes, toss with rock salt and turmeric, then fold in freshly ground mustard powder, Guntur red chilli powder, fenugreek and generous cold-pressed groundnut oil.

Keep the jar in sunlight for a few days, stirring with a dry spoon. Never use a wet spoon — moisture is the enemy of homemade pickle. Serve with hot rice and a spoon of ghee.

If you want Babai’s exact spice mix at home, try the Avakaya kit or order a ready jar of Mango Pickle (Avakaya).

title: Gongura Pickle Rice — Authentic Andhra Gongura Annam
excerpt: A handful of gongura pickle, steaming rice and ghee — the fastest Andhra comfort meal.
body:
Gongura (roselle leaves) brings a unique sour-spicy punch. Mix a spoon of Gongura Pickle into hot rice with ghee, or fold Gongura Pandu Mirchi through pulihora-style rice.

For a fuller meal, add a fried vadiyam on the side and a dollop of curd to cool the heat. This is how many Andhra households eat lunch in mango and gongura season.

title: Hair Growth Laddu — 8 Seeds and Nuts That Nourish From Within
excerpt: A traditional seed laddu packed with flax, sesame and nuts — a snack with a purpose.
body: These laddus combine flax, sesame, groundnuts and other seeds lightly roasted and bound with jaggery. Eat one a day as an evening snack. No refined sugar, no preservatives — the same small-batch approach we use for pickles.
